default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-128.title: Noise-area break from the open
E-128.hypothesis: Zarattini/Aziz/Barbon: moves from the open (or yesterday's close, whichever is farther) that stay inside the average absolute move for that minute are noise traded by liquidity providers; a close outside that band means a real supply/demand imbalance (informed or rebalancing flow) that keeps working in the same direction, so follow the first close outside the noise area.

E-129.title: Ichimoku cloud break with Tenkan/Kijun alignment
E-129.hypothesis: The Ichimoku cloud is a default overlay for many retail traders, who treat a close out of the cloud with Tenkan above Kijun as a trend start; their entries and the stops of those leaning on the cloud edge fire together at the break, so follow the first close outside the cloud when the two lines agree (mirror).

E-130.title: Multi-session price stretch fade
E-130.hypothesis: When the price sits far above its own 20-session mean (in 20-session standard deviations), swing holders are deep in profit and new multi-day buyers are scarce; the first intraday bar that closes below the previous bar's low starts their profit-taking, so fade the stretch on that counter bar (mirror).

E-132.title: DiNapoli double repo reversal
E-132.hypothesis: After a thrust of consecutive closes above the 3x3 displaced average, a close below it, a close back above and a second close below within a few bars shows the thrust buyers failing twice to resume; the late buyers of the bounce are trapped and DiNapoli users sell together, so follow the reversal (mirror).

E-133.title: Opening-gap fade in the first hours
E-133.hypothesis: A gap larger than usual is set by overnight orders placed at the open without two-sided local liquidity; once the opening orders are filled, local day traders and market makers lean back toward yesterday's close, so in the first part of the session sell each bar that closes below the previous low while price is still above yesterday's close on a gap up (mirror).

E-136.title: Inside-yesterday balance edge fade
E-136.hypothesis: While today's whole range stays inside yesterday's (after the first part of the session), the market accepts yesterday's value and nobody initiates; responsive sellers work the top part of yesterday's range and buyers the bottom, so a counter bar in the outer part of yesterday's range starts a rotation back toward its middle (mirror).

E-137.title: Midday balance break
E-137.hypothesis: From 12:00 the market trades in a low-liquidity midday balance while local desks are at lunch; when they and the US afternoon flow return, the first close outside that balance shows which side the afternoon initiative is on, and the stops resting just beyond the tight midday range push it on; follow it.
